To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the specific shear viscosity (eta/s) of QGP is small, eta/s ~ 0.1-0.2 (ii) it does not depend on the energy of the collision (iii) it does not change with the size of the colliding nuclei (iv) it does not vary significantly from one experiment to another, and (v) it does not seem to be affected by the presence of a strong magnetic field.
the specific shear viscosity of the quark-gluons plasma is (η/s) QGP = (0.08 ± 0.02) hbar/kB, and that the extracted (η/s) is consistent between RHIC and the early stage of LHC collisions.
the shear viscosity over entropy density ratio of quark-guon plasma (η/s) at RHIC and at the LHC is approximately 0.08.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the QGP properties by comparing the experimental data with the results of the VISHNU model, which is based on the hydrodynamic description of the QCD matter.
the extraction of the specific shear viscosity of the quark-gluonic plasma from experimental data and its comparison with predictions of lattice gauge theory.
the extraction of (η/s) QGP in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and at the LHC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the extracted value for (η/s) QGP is (η/s)0=0.08±0.02.
the (η/s)/T3 value for QGP is consistent with a constant, small value, independent of temperature and collision energy, and independent of the specific model assumptions.
VISHNU, together with the extracted (η/s) QGP value, provides the best description of the data from RHIC and the early LHC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can now reliably extract the (η/s)sQGP of QGP from elliptic flow measurements, and that the extracted (η/s)s QGP is surprisingly constant over a large range of collision energies.
we find no evidence for a significant energy or collision-system dependence of the specific shear viscosity of QGP.
the shear viscosity of the QGP at RHIC and LHC is small and close to the conjectured lower bound of (η/s)min = 1/(4π) for a strongly coupled fluid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the shear viscosity of the QGP at RHIC and LHC energies is small, (η/s)≃1/4π, and that the QGP at these energies can be described by a single, universal value of the shear viscosity.
the shear viscosity of the QGP at RHIC and LHC is very low, with (η/s) / 4π < 0.2.
the shear viscosity of the QGP at RHIC and LHC is small enough to allow the elliptic flow to reach the expected ideal fluid scaling.
